text: You have one free hour at the IP Week 2026 Marketplace. Where do you go first?

options.label: The booth with a complex apparatus using cutting-edge quantum fluid dynamics to predict which line at the supermarket cashier will move the fastest.
The booth with a brand name so deliciously sticky that you remember it after forgetting everything else.
The interactive installation that makes you stop, watch and immediately share it over social media.
The booth featuring a product so aesthetically exquisite it comes wrapped in hand-stitched Corinthian leather, despite being an industrial drill bit.

text: During a feverish brainstorming session, your team stumbles upon an industry-disrupting idea (an NFC-enabled hawker-table booking system that prioritises based on proximity). What do you do next?

options.label: Before the premature champagne-popping/yacht-purchasing, we do some proper research to make sure no one else has got there first.
We conclude the world is not ready for the massive societal upheaval this will cause and keep it exclusively for use in our staff canteen.
We decide the immediate priority is to brainstorm a catchy name for it before somebody defaults to 'Project Final FINAL_2'.
As part of our corporate social responsibility efforts, we open-source it for the benefit of humanity – after issuing a press release to ensure humanity knows who to thank.

text: Your primary competitor launches something that looks uncomfortably familiar to your product. What bothers you most?

options.label: They appear to have reproduced the mechanical thingamajig that makes the device work. This is inconvenient, as you had assured investors no one else would be able to.
Customers are getting confused (as customers do), despite our 47-page technical analysis painstakingly explaining the difference between the versions of Klein Blue our products are painted in.
The blurb on the back of their product box appears to be a copy of ours, including the typo that states '[insert compelling customer testimonial]'.
They have replicated a process documented only in a document title 'STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL - DO NOT CIRCULATE (Secret Process).pdf' (which was circulated extensively).

text: A prospective venture capitalist asks what makes your enterprise commercially unique. What do you lead with?

options.label: An elaborate technical breakdown of the functional apparatus, developed at the cost of several million dollars and the general mental wellbeing of the R&D team.
Years of accumulated goodwill, brand equity, and a courageous executive decision never to burden our marketing campaigns with anything recognisably related to the actual product.
Your overworked team that has produced a library worth of SOPs, training manuals, proprietary software algorithms, and instructional media that keep the entire operation running.
The product looks so exceptionally refined that customers will pay twice as much for functionality they already own, only in a less flattering shape.

text: Your organisation develops a premium new coffee plant variety. What is the grand commercial plan?

options.label: We build the entire marketing campaign around the precise misty hillside responsible for its distinctive qualities. Every burlap sack of beans comes with a complimentary dusting of the local soil and a haiku about the terroir.
Consistency is the key. Our coffee plant has been successfully bred in environments ranging from the International Space Station, the bottom of the Marianas Trench, and a McDonald's bathroom.
We greenlight a multi-movie cinematic franchise in which our brooding, anthropomorphized coffee bean leads an underground rebellion against the soulless tyranny of Instant Coffee.
We decide to share the love by cheerfully carpet-bombing seeds of our highly-invasive variety over our competitor's plantations.

text: Congratulations! Your product is objectively excellent, but sales are still lackluster. What do you think needs fixing?

options.label: Customers cannot remember its name. Neither can the writer of this personality quiz. Or you, for that matter.
Customers care about provenance. Your product's origin story begins and ends with 'manufactured somewhere with favourable overheads'.
The visual profile for your lifestyle product more closely resembles agricultural machinery.

The lion's share of the budget was spent on commissioning an original 40-second orchestral symphony that plays whenever the app opens. This has left very little money to address how frequently it crashes.

text: You have been in product development for five years and still aren't ready to go to market. What keeps you going?

options.label: The latest batch of products are consistently performing to specification without the need for the engineering team to whisper words of encouragement.
We finally proved our mechanism doesn't infringe on a patented steam-powered sausage press, despite the uncomfortable structural similarities.
We have recently achieved total operational security. The top secret proprietary process is documented nowhere and understood by no one.
You forge on in the knowledge that your work will become the foundation for the next generation. You persevere on for those who come after.

text: Your team is presenting the product at Singapore IP Week. What keeps you awake the night before?

options.label: Your lead engineer insists on presenting an AI-generated 'conceptual diagram' but nobody can agree on who owns the rights to the image, if any.
The prototype looks great from the front, but the exhibition booth permits visitors to walk around it.
The audience may fall in love with the technology, leave the auditorium and immediately buy the identical-looking knockoff from your primary competitor.
Your junior inserted confidential technical information into Slide 14 but the custom slide transitions are too elaborate to safely remove them.

text: Your business is ready to expand overseas. What is the first strategic question you think should be addressed?

options.label: How many foreign jurisdictions can we afford to ring-fence before the legal and filing fees surpass our company's valuation?
Will consumers still pay a premium if our heritage product is no longer crafted in a tiny Italian valley?
Will our business take root in foreign soil or will it wither and die on the vine?
If we gift the underlying design to the world, can we trick the entire industry into adopting it as the mandatory global standard?
